newsitem.title: USA: Florida electric chair malfunctions during execution.
newsitem.headline: Florida electric chair malfunctions during execution.

text.p: Florida's electric chair malfunctioned during an execution on Tuesday, sending a six-inch (67 cm) flame and cloud of smoke from the right side of the executed man's head, corrections officials said.

Despite the fire and smoke, prison spokeswoman Kerry Slack said the execution of Cuban immigrant Pedro Medina was not interrupted and Medina appeared to react to the lethal surges of electricity in the same way as previously executed prisoners.
Medina, 39, was pronounced dead at 7:10 a.m. (1210 GMT) at Florida State Prison near Starke.
Slack said the malfunction sent a thick cloud of smoke through the execution chamber, prompting a security officer to open a window to let out the smoke.
Medina, who spent 14 years on Florida's Death Row, was executed for the 1982 stabbing murder of an Orlando physical education teacher.
In a brief statement just before his execution Medina said: "I'm still innocent."
Archbishop Agostino Cacciavillan, apostolic pro-nuncio for Pope John Paul II, urged Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles in January for clemency for Medina but Chiles denied the request.
Since the U.S. Supreme Court reinstated the death penalty in 1976, 38 prisoners have been executed in Florida.
Medina was first scheduled to die on Dec. 5. His case was automatically delayed when his attorneys raised an insanity defence.
Some mental health experts hired by defence attorneys testified Medina was schizophrenic and brain-damaged, but several other experts appointed by the judge said he was faking to stay alive.
